story_report.summary: Pope Leo XIV began his first state visit to France in 18 years with an outdoor Mass at Paris’s Place de la Concorde, attended by an estimated 700,000 worshipers. The gathering placed a major Catholic event in a central republican space and preceded a four-day program continuing in Lourdes and Metz. French authorities designated the September 25-28 trip a “grand event,” enabling security screening within controlled areas around the Paris venue, while the visit also includes a planned private meeting with seven survivors of abuse by Catholic personnel.
